outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that on Monday, Nov 16, hourly rolling blackouts of 1 to 3 queues for all consumers, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine, tighter than Sunday's 1 to 2 queues. UNN, citing Ukrenergo, said one queue is four hours, so Monday's outages may last from 4 to 12 hours. UA.News, also citing Ukrenergo, said the Monday schedules apply throughout the day in certain regions. No later official Ukrenergo Monday schedule change was found. On Sunday afternoon, Ukrenergo said a Russian attack damaged energy equipment and that emergency power outages had been introduced in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions; energy repair crews would begin restoration work as soon as the security situation allowed. DTEK said some consumers in the cities of Dnipro and Kamianske, and in the Dnipro and Kamianske districts, were left without power, that crews were restoring supply where the security situation permitted, and that it did not give a customer count. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found for those emergency outages. Overnight outages: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said in a Nov 15 statement that a Russian attack overnight on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said crews began work once it was safe, that they were clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment, that restoration will take time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work). Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, also said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility; Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk, and reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. Prior Saturday outages with no later official restoration notice found: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on one of its facilities in the north of Odesa region on the morning of Nov 14 left almost 50,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly and that air-raid alerts were complicating the work). As of 5:30 p.m. EET Saturday, Sumyoblenergo said emergency restoration was still underway in part of Sumy region after a large-scale morning outage, and that repeated outages were possible during the work (no customer count released for security reasons). On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found.

Crews began work once it was safe, clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly, that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work, and that restoration will take time. No restoration time was given. This is a separate Nov 14 attack from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.

outages.place: Mariupol, Donetsk, Volnovakha, Novoazovsk, and nearby cities
outages.cause: Occupation authorities described an emergency in the regional power system. The Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15
outages.affected: No official customer count was given in the Nov 15 statement by the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, which said there was a partial power outage in the Donetsk, Mariupol, and Dokuchaevsk urban districts and in the Novoazovsk, Telmanove, and Volnovakha municipal districts. The ministry said crews had begun emergency restoration work and that, if conditions were favorable, a phased restoration of supply was planned by night. It also said that because of a shortage of capacity in the regional power system, supply was being limited in a number of districts, including parts of the Shakhtarsk municipal district, and that power would be restored as the system stabilized and technical conditions allowed. Vedomosti, citing the same ministry, also said that after overnight strikes on energy infrastructure, morning outages on Nov 15 had already left parts of Donetsk's Petrovskyi district, the Snizhne urban district, one settlement in the Amvrosiivka district, and part of the Yenakiieve urban district without power. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, citing Chertkov, said the first substations might return to service overnight, while other occupation authorities, including the ministry, said the damage was extensive and that it was not yet possible to determine when power would be restored. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. (RFE/RL also attributed a figure of more than 120,000 subscribers in Donetsk to the Russia-appointed mayor, Alexey Kulemzin; that figure matches a separate Nov 11 Kulemzin statement and was not included in the Nov 15 ministry statement, so it is not used here as a current count.)
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy statement via dnrnews.ru 5:01 p.m. local (= 8:01 a.m. CT) and Vedomosti; RFE/RL / Radio Svoboda report dated Nov 15; rechecked 5:57 PM CT, no later official restoration notice found

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns (Santa Cruz unit 1, Antonio Guiteras, Felton unit 2, and Renté unit 3) and maintenance (Santa Cruz unit 3, Nuevitas unit 5, Felton unit 1, and Renté unit 5); thermal generation is also limited by 251 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Sunday bulletin, published by Cubadebate and attributed to UNE-MINEM, forecast 1,860 MW affected at the evening peak: 970 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,830 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Sunday, the grid had 925 MW available versus 2,265 MW of demand, leaving 1,340 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,500 MW affected at midday. UNE said Renté unit 3 was expected to add 45 MW at the Sunday evening peak. On Saturday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Saturday affectation was 1,878 MW at 7:00 p.m. Saturday solar photovoltaic output was 3,116 MWh, with a maximum of 485 MW at midday. No official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual was found. On Sunday, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana reported generation-deficit outages of 236 MW on 101 distribution circuits at 6:00 a.m. Cuba time, and 220 MW on 105 circuits at 9:15 a.m. Cuba time, according to compilations by CiberCuba and El Alambique. CiberCuba's Nov 15 compilation also listed additional Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana generation-deficit circuit interruptions starting at 5:48 p.m. Cuba time Sunday, including circuits D1300, D1305, A1071, and GC7. The national grid was not reported as collapsed.

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation and stabilise the network after the prolonged outage. The shutdown would affect customers restored during Phase 1, including the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West. City Power also said Sentech would remain without electricity until multiple cable faults had been located and repaired. SABC News, in a 1:48 p.m. SAST Sunday report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena giving the same shutdown details. No later official notice confirming the shutdown had ended, or giving a new customer count, was found. At 9:46 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said 40% of supply had been restored to customers in Riverpark, East Bank, and Tsutsumani after an unplanned Alexandra Substation outage, and that the test branch team would be requested the next day to help locate the fault; no customer count or restoration time was given for the remainder. At 9:42 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said full supply had been restored at Florida Substation for customers in Florida Glen after an outage it said was caused by a burnt mini-substation and vandalism, reported Nov 14. At 9:39 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said a cable fault at Florida Substation's Mechanical Workshop Switching Station was affecting customers in Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia, that the team was sourcing material for repairs, and that one load centre would remain affected; the rest of that sentence was not fully available, and no customer count was given. At 7:09 p.m. SAST Sunday, City Power said that because of unforeseen challenges, the Roosevelt Substation cable-fault outage affecting parts of Emmarentia (along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield) and Greenside, reported Nov 13, would be attended to in the morning. In a 3:50 p.m. SAST Sunday Hursthill SDC bulletin, City Power said the centre was managing 1,418 open calls, 1,284 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). At 12:13 a.m. SAST Monday, City Power said operators had been notified of an outage affecting Paarlshoop and Coronationville and would be dispatched to investigate; no customer count or restoration time was given. Earlier Saturday, City Power had restored electricity to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West after overnight repairs and testing at the Hursthill and Mayfair substations, and said engineers would continue preparing for Phase 2, expected to restore remaining affected customers if there were no further technical challenges. No official Phase 2 completion notice was found. In a Saturday afternoon SABC report, City Power's Noel Maso said parts of Mayfair, Auckland Park, Crown Mines, and Vrededorp remained without power, that restoration and replacement costs stood at R24.8 million, and that in a worst-case scenario it could take up to 14 days to restore power to all affected areas.
outages.etr: City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown at Mayfair Substation would run from 12:00 noon Sunday, Nov 15 (SAST), affecting Phase 1 customers including Mayfair West, the SABC, and Netcare Garden City Hospital; no later official notice that the shutdown had ended was found. It gave no separate restoration time for remaining unrestored Mayfair-area customers or for Sentech, which it said would stay off until multiple cable faults were located and repaired. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia and Greenside, City Power said Sunday evening that the outage would be attended to in the morning. For the Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia cable-fault outage, City Power said Sunday night that the team was sourcing material for repairs and that one load centre would remain affected, and it gave no restoration time. The earlier Florida Glen outages were reported fully restored at 4:24 p.m. SAST Sunday (stolen 33 kV cable) and again at 9:42 p.m. SAST Sunday (burnt mini-substation and vandalism)

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 5:57 PM CT
